items.q: How big is the real "smart zone" for coding agents?
items.a: About **~100K tokens** regardless of a 1M nominal window — larger windows mostly add more **dumb zone**. Retrieval can use the rest; coding quality can't. Prefer **`/clear`** over compacting sediment.

items.q: What does a healthy session look like anatomically?
items.a: Tiny **system prompt** → explore → implement → test. Clearing beats compacting for predictable resets; a status line is essential for watching the smart zone.

items.q: What are the seven phases from vague Slack brief to shipped feature?
items.a: (1) **Grill Me** for shared design concept; (2) **PRD** as destination; (3) **Kanban/issues** as journey with vertical slices; (4) **AFK Ralph loop**; (5) **TDD** red-green-refactor; (6) human **QA for taste**; (7) **deep modules** + architecture skill.

items.q: Why Grill Me instead of reading a plan?
items.a: A sub-agent explore can burn ~**94K** in isolation while the parent stays lean; **22–100+** alignment questions build a shared design concept (Brooks) — after grilling, reviewing the PRD mostly tests summarization.

items.q: Why tracer-bullet vertical slices instead of horizontal layers?
items.a: AI defaults to **horizontal** coding (DB → API → UI). **Tracer bullets** give feedback before phase 3 — the first slice must span **schema + service + minimal UI**.

items.q: How does TDD stop agents from cheating?
items.a: Write a **failing test first**; use a **separate review context** so the reviewer stays in the smart zone. Without feedback loops you will **never** get decent AI output.

items.q: What runs in the Ralph AFK loop?
items.a: `once.sh` cats all **issue markdown** + last **5 commits**; permission accept-edits; the human exits the loop at implementation. Alignment stays **human-in-the-loop**; implementation can be AFK.

items.q: What codebase shape helps agents most?
items.a: **Deep modules** (Ousterhout): design interfaces, keep a mental model of gray-box implementation. Shallow modules become an **untestable graph**. Prefer closing GitHub issues over stale PRDs to avoid **doc rot**.

items.q: How does Sand Castle parallelize work?
items.a: Planner picks parallelizable issues from a **blocking DAG** → sandbox worktrees → **Sonnet** implementers → **Opus** reviewer → merger. Implementers **pull** skills; reviewers get standards **pushed**.

items.q: Where does human taste still belong?
items.a: **QA imposes your opinions** back on the codebase — automation without taste produces **slop**. One takeaway: buy the old software books (*Pragmatic Programmer*, Ousterhout).
